1.why: 5/6 and 1/24 are the two obvious operand-shaped fractions and 1/11 is a reciprocal-of-numerator trap, so 11/24 is the only value that looks like a computed result over the shared denominator 24.

2.why: -0.5/0.5/-2/2 is a complete sign-and-reciprocal cross, so every option is equally legal with the stem covered.

3.why: 10000, 100000 and 1000000 form a powers-of-ten scale ladder (classic order-of-magnitude distractor family); 650000 is the lone value carrying real information.

4.why: 12/-12 is a sign-mirror pair leaving 2 and -4 as candidates with nothing structural to separate them.

5.why: 9, 15, 21 is an arithmetic run (d=6) and 15 is its median, with 2 as the far outlier.

6.why: 8, 10, 12, 14 is a complete even run with no median and no outlier, so the set is clean.

7.why: 400, 450, 360 cluster and 150 is the outlier, but nothing inside the cluster distinguishes one value as the source.

8.why: 34, 36, 38 is a tight arithmetic run whose median is 36, and 16 is an off-scale distractor.

9.why: 392.5 is the only value carrying a decimal among 314/471/785 (all integer multiples of pi).

10.why: 28 is exactly 2x14, the classic forgot-to-halve distractor, which marks 14 as the value it was derived from.

11.why: 12, 36, 108 is a geometric run (x3) and 36 is its middle term, the others being one-step-off errors.

12.why: 2.5 is the only non-integer, and 5/8/16 are all doubling-family integers.

13.why: 35, 63, 105, 126 are all multiples of 7 with no run or derivation linking a particular one; 126 being the only even value is too weak to call.

14.why: 450, 530, 730, 820 show no run, no round-number outlier and no derivational relation.

15.why: 121 is the lone perfect square against the 11/22/44 doubling family.

16.why: Four weekday names carry no numeric or structural asymmetry at all.

17.why: 2, 3, 4, 5 is a complete consecutive run with an even count, so there is no median to favour.

19.why: 9, 15, 21 is an arithmetic run (d=6) whose median is 15; 24 sits outside it.

20.why: 12.5 is the only decimal, and 25 is exactly twice it (the forgot-to-halve twin).

21.why: 2200, 2420, 2662 is a x1.1 compound chain and 2400 is the simple-interest twin of 2420, which marks 2420 as the two-period compound result.

22.why: -2/2 is a sign mirror and 0 and 3 are unremarkable; nothing separates them.

23.why: 10 is the harmonic combination of the other two workable values (1/15 + 1/30 = 1/10), i.e. a simple arithmetic function of two other options.

24.why: 100/102/108/120 has two round values and two near-100 values with no single derivational hub.

25.why: 108 is 2x54, but doubling pairs point equally at either member, so nothing decides it.

26.why: 16, 21, 26 is an arithmetic run (d=5) with 21 as its median; 22 is the near-miss.

27.why: 7/40 is exactly half of 7/20 and 2/5 = 8/20 is its near-miss, making 7/20 the hub the other options are derived from.

28.why: 376.8, 1130.4 and 1507.2 are 1x, 3x and 4x the same base (120pi), a derived family; 904.32 is the only value outside it and the only one with two decimal places.

29.why: 84, 105, 126 is an arithmetic run (d=21) with 105 as its median; 75 is off the run.

30.why: 11/12 and 17/18 are two adjacent pairs with no outlier, round value or derivation.
